title: Version tiling and stabilized admission windows for dedicated pools
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: Upgrading dedicated GPU pools to new runtime/model builds repeatedly causes transient capacity shocks when many tenants are admitted into upgraded nodes at once. Current drain+evacuation flow relies on reactive autoscaler behaviour which allows spikes in queueing and P99 latency during waves.

This ticket proposes a two-part control: (1) version-tiling - deterministic partitioning of a pool into version tiles (small contiguous device slices) that are scheduled for upgrades in controlled waves, and (2) stabilized admission windows - a soft admission rate limiter that grants admission credits to tenants on a per-tile basis in coordination with autoscaler contracts so the autoscaler only scales when it can actually absorb traffic without breaking SLOs.
background: Related work and why this is different: many prior tickets addressed staged drains and tenant priority crediting (see dependencies). Those approaches focused on order and evasive draining heuristics. Version tiling formalizes the upgrade unit and admission windows provide a flow-control contract between rollout controller and autoscaler rather than depending solely on observed pod eviction pressure. We expect more predictable unit economics and smaller blast radius per wave.
goals: Maintain P99 inference latency degradation <= 10% during upgrades
Keep overall pool throughput drop < 8% during any single wave
Provide deterministic rollback and fast-fail criteria bound to tile-level signals
Enable operators to declare tile sizes and admission-credit budgets per rollout
non_goals: Rewriting the autoscaler internals (we will contract with it via handshake, not replace it)
Per-tenant deep admission policies (out of scope for this ticket)
proposal:
High-level flow: 1) At rollout start, controller computes version tiles for targeted pool based on shardable device ranges and tenant locality (tile size configurable, default 10% of pool capacity). 2) Controller marks tiles as staged and pre-provisions a target capacity delta we expect after upgrade (based on kernel/quantization changes). 3) For each tile, controller begins soft-drain (evict non-critical background workloads, migrate warm caches) but does not immediately admit tenant traffic. 4) Controller negotiates an 'autoscaler contract' by posting expected admission cadence and acceptance thresholds to the autoscaler endpoint; the autoscaler responds with a committed admission credit rate the pool can accept without triggering emergency scaling. 5) Controller issues admission credits to tenants in the tile at that rate. 6) Observe health signals for a stabilization window (default 10 minutes): latency p50/p95/p99, enqueue depth, GPU utilization. 7) If stable, release next tile. If not stable, pause and either reduce admission rate or roll back tile.

Implementation details: - Tile metadata stored in rollout CRD (tile_id, device_range, target_version, admission_rate, credit_balance). - A small admission proxy layer will enforce per-tenant credits and surface metrics. - Autoscaler contract is a lightweight HTTP/GRPC handshake: {pool_id, tile_id, expected_qps_delta, max_extra_instances}. Autoscaler replies with {admission_rate_per_minute, safety_token} used to validate admission flow. - Safety checks include cross-tenant rate limits and tenant priority buckets.

Trade-offs considered: - Conservative tile sizes reduce blast radius but increase total rollout time. We will expose tile size as a policy knob per pool. - Tight coupling to autoscaler API makes rollout speed dependent on autoscaler responsiveness; to mitigate we allow a graceful fallback: admission credits derived from a modeled safe rate when autoscaler is unresponsive but flagged as degraded.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end rollout on staging pool succeeds with default tile size and admission window: metrics captured and no P99 spikes >10%
Autoscaler contract validated in at least two regions (us-west, eu-central)
Runbook updated with explicit rollback decision tree and escalation path
E2E test job (k8s job) that simulates tenant admission respects credits and reproduces stable/unstable scenarios

Implement admission proxy that enforces per-tile credits (owner: Sara G.)
Extend autoscaler with contract handshake endpoint (owner: Julian)
Add metrics and dashboards: tile-level p50/p95/p99, credit burn rate, autoscaler contract health (owner: Opsguild)
Write e2e chaos test that simulates network noise and sudden tenant bursts (owner: QA)
Draft runbook and training session for oncall (owner: Priya)
Postmortem template and data collection hooks for any rollout that fails stabilization window
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards will include: per-tile latency heatmap, credit issuance and consumption graphs, autoscaler contract acceptance ratio, and admission proxy reject rate. Alerts: - TileFatal (P0): credit burn > 150% expected for 3 consecutive minutes OR p99 > 20% above baseline. - TilePauseNeeded (P1): p99 > 10% above baseline for stabilization window. - AutoscalerContractFail (P1): autoscaler rejects contracts for 2 tiles consecutively.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Canary on a single small pool in staging (tile size 5%). Phase 2: Canary in us-west production on a low-traffic dedicated pool (tile size 8%). Phase 3: Regional rollouts with adaptive tile sizes and telemetry-driven pacing. Each phase requires sign-off from SRE and Product. Default inter-tile delay: until stabilization window passes or manual override. Maximum concurrent tiles across region: 2.
rollback_criteria: Credit burn exceeds allowance and autoscaler unable to provision within 5 minutes
Significant customer error rates (5xx) correlated to tile admission for two consecutive minutes
open_questions: What is the correct default tile size for pools with many small tenants vs few large tenants? Suggest telemetry-driven default but need heuristic.
Should admission credits be transferable between tiles if a tenant is pinned to a device range?
How to expose per-tenant priority overrides without opening a DOS vector?
What SLIs will we use to tune autoscaler contract parameters in the long term?
updates: 2026-02-13: Drafted CRD schema and shared with Julian for autoscaler contract shape. Decided to keep handshake minimal to reduce coupling.
2026-02-14: Implemented prototype admission proxy in staging. Observed that naive credit windowing caused bursts at minute boundaries -> switched to token-bucket smoothing.
2026-02-16: Ops-run revealed autoscaler latency spikes under heavy metadata; added a degraded-mode that uses modeled safe rate instead of blocking rollout.
2026-02-18: PM okayed canary plan for us-west; scheduled staging canary 2026-02-20. Added runbook items and assigned oncall training. Next: finalize dashboards and complete e2e chaos tests.
